```{r package-setup}

```

## Variables

```{r variables}
# A2PA used as the sole predictor for the whole poster
x <- "A2PA"

# Outcomes compared between A2PA groups
Y <- c(
  "Age", "MMSE", "Education",
  "Current PA (WHO)", "Current PA (excl. walking, chores)", "Current PA (excl. walking, chores, gardening)",
  "SA",
  "RAVLR-DR", "z(RAVLT-DR)",
  "TMT-B", "z(TMT-B)",
  "BNT-30", "z(BNT-30)", "Animal naming", "z(Animal naming)",
  "GDS-15", "Prob. depression", "GAI-SF", "Prob. anxiety", "FAQ",
  "Mental activities",
  "BMI", "Subj. health", "Smoking", "Alcohol", "Hypertension", "Diabetes"
)
```

## Data

```{r data-import}
# NOTE: data live in a freeze artifact at OSF
raw_data <- midphysac::read_poster_data()

# NOTE: data are trimmed at A2PA < 4 for this analysis
df <- filter(raw_data, A2PA <= "Active")
```

# 1 · The sample (row 1, column 2)

```{r sample-palette}
# Poster palette. Athlete / Enthusiast / Active carry the group colours used in
# every panel; everything below the third level is greyed to mark exclusion.
pal  <- c(Athlete = "#22415C", Enthusiast = "#D19A2E", Active = "#3F8E8C")
grey <- "#6E7C8C"
ink  <- "#1E2833"
hair <- "#C3D2DE"

# Row fills are the same hues mixed 15 % over white. col2rgb() returns colours
# in COLUMNS, rgb() wants them in ROWS, hence the transpose.
tint <- function(x, p = 0.15) {
  grDevices::rgb(t(p * grDevices::col2rgb(x) + (1 - p) * 255), maxColorValue = 255)
}
```

```{r sample-table}
# All five A2PA levels, including the two that the analyses exclude.
sample_rows <-
  raw_data |>
  summarise(
    N    = n(),
    Age  = sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", mean(Age,  na.rm = TRUE), sd(Age,  na.rm = TRUE)),
    MMSE = sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", mean(MMSE, na.rm = TRUE), sd(MMSE, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .by  = A2PA
  ) |>
  arrange(A2PA) |>
  mutate(A2PA = as.character(A2PA))

# Accent per row: palette for the analysed levels, grey for the rest.
n_keep <- length(pal)
accent <- c(unname(pal), rep(grey, nrow(sample_rows) - n_keep))
fills  <- tint(accent)

# Education is stated in the note rather than given a column.
edu_range <-
  df |>
  summarise(higher = mean(Education == "higher", na.rm = TRUE), .by = A2PA) |>
  pull(higher) |>
  range()

sample_rows
```

```{r sample-gt}
tab_sample <-
  sample_rows |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_label(A2PA = "A2PA identity", N = "N", Age = "Age", MMSE = "MMSE") |>
  gt::cols_align("left",  columns = A2PA) |>
  gt::cols_align("center", columns = c(N, Age, MMSE)) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(color = grey, weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_column_labels()
  )

# Row-wise colour coding. A left rule in the full-strength hue carries the code
# even in greyscale; the fill is a quiet second cue.
for (i in seq_len(nrow(sample_rows))) {
  tab_sample <-
    tab_sample |>
    gt::tab_style(
      style = list(
        gt::cell_fill(color = fills[i]),
        gt::cell_text(color = if (i <= n_keep) ink else grey)
      ),
      locations = gt::cells_body(rows = i)
    ) |>
    gt::tab_style(
      style = list(
        gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
        gt::cell_borders(sides = "left", color = accent[i], weight = gt::px(10))
      ),
      locations = gt::cells_body(columns = A2PA, rows = i)
    )
}

tab_sample <-
```

# 2 · The activity ladder (row 2, column 1)

```{r activity-ladder-plot}
# ---- 2 · The activity ladder (row 2, column 1) -------------------------------

## ---- r ladder-data ----
pa_levels <- c(
  "Current PA (WHO)",
  "Current PA (excl. walking, chores)",
  "Current PA (excl. walking, chores, gardening)"
)

# NOTE: WHO is the demanding criterion: it needs BOTH moderate-or-intense
# intensity AND >= 2.5 h/week. The other two need only > 0 hours, at any
# intensity of a progressively narrower list of activity types.
pa_label <- c(
  "WHO-recommended\nphysical activity",
  "Any PA excluding\nwalking and chores",
  "Any PA excluding\nwalking, chores and gardening"
)

ladder <-
  df |>
  select(A2PA, all_of(pa_levels)) |>
  pivot_longer(-A2PA, names_to = "measure", values_to = "meets") |>
  mutate(meets = as.integer(as.character(meets))) |>
  summarise(k = sum(meets), n = n(), .by = c(A2PA, measure)) |>
  mutate(
    # Wilson score interval = prop.test(correct = FALSE);
    # Wald is unusable here because 91/92 pushes its upper limit past 100 %.
    p  = 100 * k / n,
    lo = 100 * map2_dbl(k, n, \(k, n) prop.test(k, n, correct = FALSE)$conf.int[1]),
    hi = 100 * map2_dbl(k, n, \(k, n) prop.test(k, n, correct = FALSE)$conf.int[2]),
    m_i   = match(measure, pa_levels),
    label = factor(pa_label[m_i], levels = pa_label),
    A2PA  = factor(as.character(A2PA), levels = names(pal))
  )

## ---- r ladder-tests ----
ladder_tests <-
  ladder |>
  arrange(m_i, A2PA) |>
  summarise(tab = list(cbind(yes = k, no = n - k)), .by = c(m_i, measure)) |>
  arrange(m_i) |>
  mutate(
    chi     = map(tab, \(t) suppressWarnings(chisq.test(t))),
    X2      = map_dbl(chi, \(x) unname(x$statistic)),
    dfree   = map_dbl(chi, \(x) unname(x$parameter)),
    p_chi   = map_dbl(chi, \(x) x$p.value),
    min_exp = map_dbl(chi, \(x) min(x$expected)),  # < 5 invalidates the approximation
    p_fish  = map_dbl(tab, \(t) fisher.test(t)$p.value)
  )

# APA-style bounded statistic: strip the leading zero.
no0 <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x))
}
fmt_p  <- function(p) if (p < .001) "*p* < .001" else sprintf("*p* = %s", no0(p, 3))
fmt_x2 <- function(i) {
  with(ladder_tests[i, ],
       sprintf("&#967;<sup>2</sup>(%d) = %s, %s", dfree, no0(X2, 1), fmt_p(p_chi)))
}

## ---- r ladder-plot ----
FAM <- "Helvetica Neue"
Y0  <- 50
SHP <- c(Athlete = 21, Enthusiast = 22, Active = 24) # secondary encoding

ladder_finding <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "**A2PA identity indicates what the women do, not how much.**",
    "Meeting the WHO-recommended level does not separate the groups (%s);",
    "doing any activity beyond walking and chores does (%s),",
    "and excluding gardening widens the gap (%s)."
  ),
  fmt_x2(1),
  fmt_x2(2),
  fmt_x2(3)
)

ladder_how <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "All three panels score the same %d women.",
    "WHO criterion counts at least 2.5 h/week of moderate or vigorous activity of any type;",
    "the other two count any amount at any intensity, of a narrowing list of types.",
    "Dots are proportions, bars 95%% Wilson intervals, axis truncated at %d%%.",
    "Smallest expected count in the middle panel is %s. Fisher's exact test agree with &#967;<sup>2</sup> (*p* = %s)."
  ),
  sum(ladder$n[ladder$m_i == 1]),
  Y0,
  no0(ladder_tests$min_exp[2], 1),
  no0(ladder_tests$p_fish[2], 3)
)

p_ladder <-
  ggplot(
    ladder,
    aes(x = A2PA, y = p, colour = A2PA)
  ) +
  geom_linerange(
    aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
    linewidth = 2.8,
    alpha = 0.45,
    lineend = "round"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = A2PA, shape = A2PA),
    size = 8.5,
    colour = "white",
    stroke = 1.8
  ) +
  # Every point is labelled: the two near-identical WHO values sit at different
  # x positions, so their labels separate horizontally.
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.0f %%", p)),
    nudge_x = 0.25,
    hjust = 0,
    size = 25 / .pt,
    fontface = "bold",
    colour = ink,
    family = FAM
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ label,
    nrow = 1
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = pal,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = pal,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = SHP,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.55, 1.5))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(Y0, 100),
    breaks = seq(Y0, 100, 10),
    labels = \(v) paste0(v, " %"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.03, 0.05))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Percentage of women meeting the criterion",
    caption = paste(ladder_finding, ladder_how)
  ) +
  # colour, fill and shape all map to A2PA, so ggplot merges them into one
  # legend; override.aes must be given once or it warns about duplication.
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 9, stroke = 1.8))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 26,
    base_family = FAM
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = hair, linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.spacing.x    = unit(26, "pt"),
    strip.text   = element_text(
      size = 24,
      face = "bold",
      colour = ink,
      lineheight = 1.15,
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(b = 12)
    ),
    axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(colour = grey, size = 24),
    axis.title.y = element_text(colour = grey, size = 24, margin = margin(r = 10)),
    axis.ticks   = element_blank(),
    # Bottom-centre of the plotting region, which is the middle facet.
    # ggplot2 >= 3.5 wants legend.position = "inside" + legend.position.inside.
    legend.position      = c(0.5, 0.02),
    legend.justification = c(0.5, 0),
    legend.direction     = "horizontal",
    legend.background    = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    legend.text   = element_text(size = 26, face = "bold", colour = ink),
    legend.margin = margin(4, 8, 4, 8),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    # Wrapping caption, following the ECVP builder's two-tier convention.
    plot.caption = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(
      size = 22, colour = grey, family = FAM, lineheight = 1.3,
      margin = margin(t = 18), halign = 0
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(6, 10, 4, 4)
  )

p_ladder
```

# 3 · Cognition (row 2, column 2)

```{r cognition-plot}
# ---- 3 · Cognition (row 2, column 2) -----------------------------------------

## ---- r cognition-data ----
# The four domains that define SuperAging. Memory first: it is the finding.
z_levels <- c("z(RAVLT-DR)", "z(TMT-B)", "z(BNT-30)", "z(Animal naming)")
z_label  <- c("Delayed recall", "TMT-B", "BNT-30", "Animal naming")

domains <-
  df |>
  select(A2PA, all_of(z_levels)) |>
  pivot_longer(-A2PA, names_to = "domain", values_to = "z") |>
  filter(!is.na(z)) |>
  mutate(
    d_i    = match(domain, z_levels),
    domain = factor(z_label[d_i], levels = z_label),
    A2PA   = factor(as.character(A2PA), levels = names(pal))
  )

# Mean and 95 % CI per group and domain, following the convention of the
# earlier COSACTIW poster: violin = distribution, dot = mean, bar = 95 % CI.
domain_mean <-
  domains |>
  summarise(
    m  = mean(z),
    se = sd(z) / sqrt(n()),
    n  = n(),
    .by = c(domain, A2PA)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    lo = m - qt(.975, n - 1) * se,
    hi = m + qt(.975, n - 1) * se
  )

# SuperAging prevalence
sa <-
  df |>
  summarise(
    k     = sum(SA == "1", na.rm = TRUE),
    n     = sum(!is.na(SA)),
    n_all = n(),
    .by   = A2PA
  ) |>
  mutate(
    p  = 100 * k / n,
    lo = 100 * map2_dbl(k, n, \(k, n) prop.test(k, n, correct = FALSE)$conf.int[1]),
    hi = 100 * map2_dbl(k, n, \(k, n) prop.test(k, n, correct = FALSE)$conf.int[2]),
    A2PA = factor(as.character(A2PA), levels = names(pal))
  )

## ---- r cognition-tests ----
# One-way ANOVA per domain with Tukey HSD post-hoc
domain_tests <-
  domains |>
  nest_by(domain) |>
  mutate(
    fit  = list(aov(z ~ A2PA, data = data)),
    tidy = list(summary(fit)[[1]]),
    `F`  = tidy[["F value"]][1],
    df1  = tidy[["Df"]][1],
    df2  = tidy[["Df"]][2],
    p    = tidy[["Pr(>F)"]][1],
    pw   = list(TukeyHSD(fit)$A2PA)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(domain, `F`, df1, df2, p, pw)

sa_test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(cbind(sa$k, sa$n - sa$k)))

# Pairwise p-values for the memory domain, Enthusiast against the other two.
# TukeyHSD names rows "<second>-<first>" in factor-level order.
mem_pw <- domain_tests$pw[[1]]
stopifnot(all(c("Enthusiast-Athlete", "Active-Enthusiast") %in% rownames(mem_pw)))
p_ath  <- mem_pw["Enthusiast-Athlete", "p adj"]
p_act  <- mem_pw["Active-Enthusiast", "p adj"]

# Vectorised: these are called inside mutate() over all four domains.
fmt_p  <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "*p* < .001", sprintf("*p* = %s", no0(p, 3)))
fmt_pp <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "p < .001",   sprintf("p = %s",   no0(p, 3)))
fmt_F  <- function(i) {
  with(domain_tests[i, ],
       sprintf("*F*(%d, %d) = %s, %s", df1, df2, no0(F, 2), fmt_p(p)))
}

## ---- r cognition-plot ----
Z_BOT <- min(domains$z, na.rm = TRUE)
BR    <- Z_BOT - 0.45
LAB   <- 0.10   # gap between line and label top
STAG  <- 1.10   # vertical offset of the second bracket

mem_brackets <- data.frame(
  domain = factor(z_label[1], levels = z_label),
  x      = c(1, 2),
  xend   = c(2, 3),
  y      = c(BR, BR - STAG),
  lab    = c(fmt_pp(p_ath), fmt_pp(p_act))
)

# Pairwise differences in SuperAging prevalence, with Newcombe-style intervals
# from the same prop.test family as the proportions themselves.
CL <- 1 - 0.05 / 3   # Bonferroni level for three pairwise contrasts

sa_pairs <- data.frame(
  a = c("Enthusiast", "Enthusiast", "Athlete"),
  b = c("Athlete", "Active", "Active")
) |>
  mutate(
    lab = paste(a, "-", b),
    d   = map2_dbl(a, b, \(a, b) {
      i <- match(c(a, b), sa$A2PA)
      100 * (sa$k[i[1]] / sa$n[i[1]] - sa$k[i[2]] / sa$n[i[2]])
    }),
    # Bonferroni level for the three contrasts, so "interval excludes zero" IS
    # the adjusted test and the colour cue cannot contradict the geometry.
    lo = map2_dbl(a, b, \(a, b) {
      i <- match(c(a, b), sa$A2PA)
      100 * prop.test(sa$k[i], sa$n[i], correct = FALSE, conf.level = CL)$conf.int[1]
    }),
    hi = map2_dbl(a, b, \(a, b) {
      i <- match(c(a, b), sa$A2PA)
      100 * prop.test(sa$k[i], sa$n[i], correct = FALSE, conf.level = CL)$conf.int[2]
    }),
    sig = lo > 0 | hi < 0
  ) |>
  mutate(lab = factor(lab, levels = rev(lab)))

p_sa <-
  ggplot(
    sa,
    aes(x = A2PA, y = p, colour = A2PA)
  ) +
  geom_linerange(
    aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
    linewidth = 2.8,
    alpha = 0.45,
    lineend = "round"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = A2PA, shape = A2PA),
    size = 8.5,
    colour = "white",
    stroke = 1.8
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.0f %%", p)),
    nudge_x = 0.22,
    hjust = 0,
    size = 25 / .pt,
    fontface = "bold",
    colour = ink,
    family = FAM
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = pal,
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = pal,
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = SHP,
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 1.1))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = \(v) paste0(v, " %"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.18, 0.18))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    subtitle = "SuperAging"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 26,
    base_family = FAM
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = hair, linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(colour = grey, size = 23),
    axis.ticks   = element_blank(),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 25,
      face = "bold",
      colour = ink,
      margin = margin(b = 6),
      hjust = 0.5
    )
  )

p_sa_diff <-
  ggplot(
    sa_pairs,
    aes(x = d, y = lab)
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    colour = grey,
    linewidth = 0.7,
    linetype = "22"
  ) +
  geom_linerange(
    aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, colour = sig),
    linewidth = 2.8,
    alpha = 0.45,
    lineend = "round"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(colour = sig, shape = sig),
    size = 7,
    fill = "white",
    stroke = 1.8
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(`TRUE` = ink, `FALSE` = grey),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(`TRUE` = 19, `FALSE` = 21),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = scales::breaks_width(20),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.12, 0.12))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    subtitle = "Pairwise difference (pp)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 26,
    base_family = FAM
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = hair, linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(colour = ink, size = 23, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.x  = element_text(colour = grey, size = 23),
    axis.ticks   = element_blank(),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 25,
      face = "bold",
      colour = ink,
      margin = margin(b = 6),
      hjust = 0.5
    )
  )

p_dom <-
  ggplot(
    domains,
    aes(x = A2PA, y = z)
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    colour = grey,
    linewidth = 0.7,
    linetype = "22"
  ) +
  geom_violin(
    aes(fill = A2PA, colour = A2PA),
    alpha = 0.30,
    linewidth = 1.1,
    width = 0.9,
    trim = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_linerange(
    data = domain_mean,
    aes(y = m, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, colour = A2PA),
    linewidth = 2.8,
    lineend = "round"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = domain_mean,
    aes(y = m, fill = A2PA, shape = A2PA),
    size = 7,
    colour = "white",
    stroke = 1.6
  ) +
  # Memory only; annotate() ignores `data`, so these need their own facet key.
  geom_segment(
    data = mem_brackets,
    aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = ink,
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = mem_brackets,
    aes(x = (x + xend) / 2, y = y - LAB, label = lab),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 22 / .pt,
    colour = ink,
    family = FAM
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ domain,
    nrow = 1
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = pal,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = pal,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = SHP,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.26, 0.05))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Domain z score"
  ) +
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 9, stroke = 1.8, alpha = 1))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 26,
    base_family = FAM
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = hair, linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.spacing.x    = unit(20, "pt"),
    strip.text   = element_text(
      size = 25,
      face = "bold",
      colour = ink,
      hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(b = 10)
    ),
    axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(colour = grey, size = 23),
    axis.title.y = element_text(colour = grey, size = 23, margin = margin(r = 8)),
    axis.ticks   = element_blank(),
    legend.position      = "bottom",
    legend.direction     = "horizontal",
    legend.text   = element_text(size = 26, face = "bold", colour = ink),
    legend.margin = margin(t = 4)
  )

cog_finding <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "**Enthusiasts reach SuperAging about twice as often,",
    "courtesy of their superior memory.**",
    "SuperAging prevalence differs betweeen groups (%s);",
    "delayed recall separates them (%s) while the other three domains do not (all *p* > %s)."
  ),
  sprintf(
    "&#967;<sup>2</sup>(%d) = %s, %s",
    sa_test$parameter,
    no0(unname(sa_test$statistic), 1),
    fmt_p(sa_test$p.value)
  ),
  fmt_F(1),
  no0(min(domain_tests$p[-1]), 2)
)

# Denominators are computed, not assumed: SA and the domain scores each have
# their own missingness.
n_dom <- range(summarise(domain_mean, n = sum(n), .by = domain)$n)

cog_how <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "Violins represent z-score distributions against the appropriate norms, dot the mean,",
    "bar its 95%% CI; the dashed line is the normative average.",
    "Pairwise differences in prevalence (top right) show %.1f%% intervals, Bonferroni",
    "adjusted for the three contrasts, so a filled mark indicate statistically significant differences.",
    "Domain post-hoc contrasts presented in the Delayed recall panel are Tukey HSDs.",
    "SuperAging is defined *by* the four presented domains, so the lower",
    "row explains the upper one rather than confirming it independently.",
    "Of %d women, SuperAging status was determinable for %d and domain scores",
    "for %s."
  ),
  100 * CL,
  nrow(df),
  sum(sa$n),
  if (n_dom[1] == n_dom[2]) sprintf("%d", n_dom[1])
  else sprintf("%d to %d depending on domain", n_dom[1], n_dom[2])
)

p_cognition <-
  patchwork::wrap_plots(
    patchwork::wrap_plots(p_sa, p_sa_diff, ncol = 2, widths = c(1, 1.3)),
    p_dom,
    ncol = 1, heights = c(1, 2.3)
  ) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    caption = paste(cog_finding, cog_how),
    theme = theme(
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      plot.caption = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(
        size = 22,
        colour = grey,
        family = FAM,
        lineheight = 1.3,
        margin = margin(t = 14),
        halign = 0
      ),
      plot.margin = margin(6, 10, 4, 4)
    )
  )

p_cognition
```
